documentTitle: Matcha On Ice Cafe — Coffee Bar Manual

sections.label: Espresso Basics
sections.blurb: Dose, yield and extraction time — the shot every espresso classic and Signature Coffee is built from.

story.heading: Pulling a Shot
body: Espresso is brewed by forcing hot water through finely-ground, tamped coffee under pressure — roughly 9 bars — extracting a concentrated shot with a layer of golden crema on top.

Every espresso-based drink in this manual starts from the same double shot: 2 oz, pulled to land in a 25–30 second window. Dial the grind in against that window, not the clock alone — finer if it runs fast and sour, coarser if it runs slow and bitter.

callout.label: Extraction Time
callout.note: Adjust grind size until the shot lands in this window at your standard dose.

method: Dose and distribute the ground coffee evenly in the portafilter basket.
Tamp level and firm, straight down.
Lock in and start the shot immediately — don't let it sit.
Time the extraction from the first drop; stop at 2 oz.
Adjust the grind size, not the dose, to hit the window.

sections.label: Espresso Classics
sections.blurb: The standard bar drinks — same double shot, different milk and water.

drinks.name: Espresso
method: Pull a double shot directly into the serving cup.
Serve immediately, while the crema is still fresh.
Discard and re-pull if the shot didn't land in the 25–30 second window.
drinks.note: No milk, no water — just the shot. The purest test of a dial-in.

drinks.name: Americano
method: Add hot water to the cup first.
Pull the double shot on top of the water.
Adjust the water for a stronger or lighter cup.
drinks.note: Water first, then espresso on top — pulling the shot before the water breaks up the crema.

drinks.name: Macchiato
method: Pull a double shot into the serving cup.
Steam a small amount of milk to a thick foam.
Spoon a dollop of foam onto the shot — don't stir it in.
drinks.note: Macchiato means "marked" — the foam should mark the surface, not drown the shot.

drinks.name: Cortado
method: Pull a double shot into the serving cup or glass.
Steam milk to a silky texture with minimal foam.
Pour in milk to roughly match the espresso, equal parts.
drinks.note: Cortado means "cut" — the milk cuts the espresso's acidity without floating on top like foam.

drinks.name: Flat White
method: Pull a double shot into the serving cup.
Steam milk to a thin, velvety microfoam — about 0.5 cm.
Pour in a steady stream, integrating the microfoam rather than floating it on top.
drinks.note: Less milk and less foam than a latte — the espresso should still lead.

drinks.name: Cappuccino
method: Pull a double shot into the serving cup.
Steam milk to a thick, airy foam.
Pour to fill, finishing with a full foam cap.
drinks.note: Traditionally close to equal thirds — espresso, steamed milk, foam.

drinks.name: Latte
method: Pull a double shot into the serving cup.
Steam milk to a thin microfoam — about 0.5 cm.
Pour to fill, finishing with a thin foam layer.
drinks.note: The most milk-forward of the classics — a mellow, rounded cup.
